title: Dragon Ball: Yo! Son Goku and His Friends Return!!
summary: A ~34-minute festival short screened at the Jump Super Anime Tour '08 for Weekly Shōnen Jump's 40th anniversary — premiered 2008-09-21 at the Grand Cube Osaka and toured to 2008-11-23 (Kanzenshuu's feature page lists ten dated screenings; ja-WP says 全国11会場), never broadcast, later given away on a mail-order DVD and included in the Battle of Gods Special Limited Edition box (2013-09-13). Against this owner's instrument — Toriyama's Dragon Ball manga, ch 1-519, finished 1995 — it is an ORIGINAL and adapts nothing: ja-WP calls it flatly 「「ジャンプスーパーアニメツアー08」で上映されたオリジナル作品」, Toriyama supplied the 原案 (scenario draft) and the character designs while 小山高生 wrote the screenplay (ja-WP infobox 監督 上田芳裕 / 脚本 小山高生 / 原案 鳥山明 / 原作 鳥山明; Kanzenshuu's production credits print the same three lines) — the exact credit shape the applied dragon-ball-z triage calls 'a credit that is not an adoption' across 18/18 originals on this shelf. It even contradicts the manga: ja-WP records that here the general public knows about Buu, 「原作では、神龍の力で一般の人々からブウの記憶は消されているが…原作やテレビアニメとは異なる点がある」. Filler (T27), no chapters (A1), no adoption. THE TRAP THE TASK NAMES IS REAL AND POINTS THE OTHER WAY: the 2009 manga of the same title is Naho Ooishi's two-part COMICALIZATION of this short (V-Jump 2009年5月号・6月号 as a bound-in appendix, supervised by Toriyama; a separate JSAT anime comic followed on 2010-09-03) — an adaptation OF the special, in no chapter space of this instrument. THE VERDICT IS THE SLOT: the story is 「魔人ブウ編から約2年後」 (Age 776), inside the ten-year gap the manga leaves between ch 517 and ch 518, and it is the EARLIEST of the three works now in that gap — the wiki's Battle of Gods page says so in as many words, and ja-WP's 神と神 carries the same in-film reference (Bulma naming Vegeta's brother Tarble, the special's own guest character). So the DBZ cluster reads Yo! Son Goku (776) → Battle of Gods (778) → Resurrection 'F' (779), and this row asks for the first seat.

position.why: CORRECTED 291.53 → 288.5. (1) THE GAP: the short is set about two years after Kid Buu's defeat — ja-WP 「魔人ブウ編から約2年後の物語」, the wiki 'about two years after the defeat of Kid Buu. Therefore, it is set in Age 776' — i.e. inside the ten years the manga skips between ch 517 (the Buu fight ends) and ch 518 (the 28th Budokai, Age 784); Toei's own Battle of Gods release names that gap: 「原作517話で魔人ブウとの戦いが終わった後、518話までの空白の10年」. (2) THE ROWS, BY TITLE + DATE (R20): the gap falls between ep 288 遅いぜ悟空！みんなでパーティ!! / 'He's Always Late' (1996-01-10, filler, no anchor) and ep 289 悟空おじいちゃん！私がパンよ!! / 'Granddaughter Pan' (1996-01-17 → ch 517-518, ten years later) — en-WP's Dragon Ball Z season 9 matches our grid title for title and date for date. (3) THE FIRST SEAT: the wiki's Battle of Gods page places the two works relative to each other — 'It also takes place after the events of Dragon Ball: The Return of Son Goku and Friends!, which is set two years after Kid Buu's defeat, as Bulma references Tarble' — and ja-WP 神と神 records the same reference inside that film (ブルマから弟（ターブル）の存在を指摘された). Release order agrees (2008-09-21 < 2013-03-30 < 2015-04-18), so there is no story-vs-release fork here: both orders read Yo! → BoG → RoF. The stored 291.53 is only the air-date derivation (2008 against a 1996 finale). COST, STATED PLAINLY: giving this row 288.5 RE-RULES Battle of Gods 288.5 → 288.51 (Sean, 2026-09-06) and moves Resurrection 'F' to 288.52. If you prefer to leave BoG at 288.5, this row becomes 288.52 behind RoF at 288.51 — the cluster then displays the earliest work last; a third way is 288.05 (the slime 24.05 precedent), which keeps both orders and touches nothing.

flags_for_sean: FLAG 1 — THE 288.5x CLUSTER IS ONE RULING FOR THREE ROWS, AND THIS ROW IS THE ONE THAT COSTS A RE-RULING. All three works sit in the ch 517/518 gap and STORY ORDER AND RELEASE ORDER AGREE on their sequence: Yo! Son Goku (Age 776; 2008-09-21) → Battle of Gods (778; 2013-03-30) → Resurrection 'F' (779; 2015-04-18). OPTION A (delivered): Yo! 288.5 · BoG 288.51 · RoF 288.52 — right in both orders; cost: BoG's 288.5, ruled 2026-09-06, becomes 288.51. OPTION B (leave BoG untouched): BoG 288.5 · RoF 288.51 · Yo! 288.52 — cost: the earliest work displays last (E13's cluster-order audit skips ruled rows, so nothing would catch it — the display would simply be wrong). OPTION C: Yo! 288.05 · BoG 288.5 · RoF 288.51 — both orders right, no re-ruling, at the price of a sub-.5 seat; precedented once (that-time-i-got-reincarnated-as-a-slime 106509 @24.05, ruled to sit ahead of the wiki row @24.1).

FLAG 2 — MECHANICS: 288.5 IS HELD TODAY, SO THE TWO ROWS MUST BE RULED TOGETHER. planRuledMoves lets a mover take a slot another mover is leaving, but REFUSES a ruled slot held by a row that is not moving (the kinnikuman 3276 lesson: the mover keeps its stored position and the census lists stored ≠ ruled). Under Option A, Battle of Gods must carry its new 288.51 in the SAME apply as this row's 288.5. Options B and C contest nothing (288.52 / 288.05 are free; 291.53 is emptied either way).

FLAG 3 — NO ADOPTION, AND THE CREDIT SHAPE IS THE SHELF'S OWN PATTERN. 脚本 小山高生; Toriyama is 原作 (the franchise line) and 原案 (the scenario draft) and drew the character designs — Tarble, Gure, Abo and Kado. The applied dragon-ball-z triage (out/triage__dragon-ball-z.json, 18/18 originals) reads exactly this shape as 'the T26 shape of a credit that is not an adoption', and nothing entered the manga: it had been finished for thirteen years. This is the nineteenth original on that shelf (twentieth with Battle of Gods).

FLAG 4 — THE COMICALIZATION IS AN ADAPTATION OF THE SPECIAL, NEVER AN INSTRUMENT. Naho Ooishi's two-part 『ドラゴンボール オッス!帰ってきた孫悟空と仲間たち!!』 ran as a bound-in appendix in V-Jump 2009年5月号 and 6月号 under Toriyama's supervision (ja-WP; en-WP dates the two parts 2009-03-21 and 2009-04-21; the wiki says they were collected in a single volume on 2010-09-10), and a separate JSAT anime comic followed on 2010-09-03. No mainline chapter number, no place in ch 1-519 — never a chapter to cite and never a reason to read this row as adapting anything.

FLAG 5 — A CONTINUITY CLAUSE WORTH ONE LINE IN THE NOTE. ja-WP records that the special contradicts the source it sits inside: 「原作では、神龍の力で一般の人々からブウの記憶は消されているが、本作ではブウのことを一般人が認知している」. It is franchise-adjacent and Toriyama-plotted, but it is not the manga's own line — which is the same distinction the 正史 clause makes for the two modern films.

FLAG 6 — STORED KIND AND DATE HOLD; NO REPAIR PROPOSED. `special` is right for an event-screened short (Kanzenshuu files it under 'Festival Features'; ja-WP calls it 「特別編アニメ」; the wiki's 'third Dragon Ball Z OVA' is a home-video reading of the mail-order DVD, not the screening). The date 2008-09-21 is the Osaka premiere; the tour ran to 2008-11-23, so a stored single date is the premiere, correctly. Runtime is reported as 33 (the wiki) / ~34 (Kanzenshuu) / 35 minutes (ja-WP, en-WP) — we store none.

FLAG 7 — SHELF PARITY, OUT OF SCOPE BUT WORTH ONE LINE: dragon-ball-z-kai re-cuts the same manga through the same gap and holds Battle of Gods (165.5) and Resurrection 'F' (165.51 proposed), but the halo never staged this special there. If you want the Kai shelf to read the same story, its seat would be 165.5 with the other two moving up a hundredth — an I45 staging question, not this verdict's.
